title: Commitment handoff and regional ops playbook review
summary: Quarterly renewal / expansion check-in: customer confirms intent to extend retainer and add EU region plus an APAC burst window. Discussed dedicated capacity vs hosted burst, VPC/KMS requirements, latency targets, and timeline for contract amendment. Agreed to run a perf soak test next week and share pricing amendment by end of week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-17
Time: 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Maya Chen, Daniel Ortiz, Priya Malhotra
Attendees (Customer): Raj Patel, Sofia Mendes, Luke Harper, Aisha Noor

--- Auto summary (brief) ---
Ivyline is leaning toward a 12-month retainer extension with a committed EU region (private VPC) and an APAC burst pool for holiday season. They want a clear operational runbook and a perf test before signing. Security and KMS integration are gating items.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. we wanted to run through the handoff and ops playbook for the renewal and the regional pieces. is this a good time?
[00:12] Raj: yep, all good. quick note from my side — our capacity forecast showed a 2.5x token peak in q4 if marketing push lands, hence the APAC burst ask.
[00:23] Daniel: cool, that matches what we saw in the pre-check numbers. couple things to call out — dedicated pools for EU are straightforward, we can provision a private VPC cluster, tie to your KMS. APAC burst we usually handle with a reserved burst pool on hosted infra or a scheduled capacity bump. tradeoffs on latency/cost there.
[00:42] Sofia: when you say "private VPC cluster" — do we get full control over egress rules and peering? our security team requires peering through transit gateway.
[00:51] Maya: yes, you can peer via transit gateway, we support customer-managed peering. there was a note in the SOC doc about supported topologies — we'll share the network diagram after this.
[01:03] Luke: and what about KMS? we need HSM-backed keys, not just cloud KMS. is that supported?
[01:08] Daniel: short answer: yes. we integrate with external KMS/HSM providers via our private control plane. there's a little ops work on both sides to map key aliases, but it's been done in prior pilots. we can put the exact checklist in the runbook.
[01:22] Raj: good. next — can you run through latency targets if we move EU to private? we need <60ms p99 for our UI flows, otherwise we have to keep a local cache.
[01:33] Daniel: private EU will get you closer to 40–55ms p99 depending on model and sequence length. two caveats: model selection (quantized vs fp16) and batching policy matter a lot. if you need 40ms consistently we'll recommend a dedicated pool with lower batching and higher concurrency — that increases unit cost.
[01:54] Sofia: ok so that's the classic latency vs cost trade. our ops lead will want numbers in a spreadsheet — can you provide cost delta examples for 40ms vs 60ms?
[02:03] Maya: yep, we'll send a delta worksheet. we'll include a few profiles (gen-heavy, chat-heavy) and the recommended config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization).
[02:13] Aisha: procurement question — if we sign a 12-month amendment, can we front-load some committed capacity for the APAC burst credits? we prefer committed credits we can draw down.
[02:23] Priya: yes we can structure a commit + burst arrangement, there are two models — reserved credits with scheduled bursts or a true burst pool billed overage. we'll put both options in the amendment.
[02:35] Luke: timeline — we want the runbook and pricing by Friday, then a perf soak next Tues/Wed, and sign by April 30 if benchmarks are good. is that realistic?
[02:46] Maya: it's tight but doable. we'll aim to get the pricing and ops doc by Friday COB, Daniel will book the soak window with Sofia for Tues.
[02:57] Raj: one more — compliance: we need audit logs to be retained 2 years and an access log stream to our SIEM. can Redwood support that retention/streaming?
[03:08] Daniel: yes, we've done two-year exports; we can stream events to your SIEM (syslog/kinesis) and configure retention. we'll need the SIEM endpoint and schema.
[03:20] Sofia: we'll share endpoints. also: our infra team wants a dry-run of the peering and a canary before full cutover.
[03:29] Daniel: absolutely, the playbook will include a canary plan and rollback steps.
[03:36] Raj: any blockers from your side? costs aside, any limitations on model variants we'd run in private?
[03:44] Maya: most open models we host in private; some very new model builds may require kernel tuning that we can provision but needs an extra validation cycle — we'll flag any model-specific constraints in the plan.
[03:57] Luke: competitors — we've been talking to CloudServeAI and FastServe; they offered a cheaper burst option but no private KMS integration yet. just flagging.
[04:09] Maya: good to know, thanks. we think the KMS + ops playbook is where Redwood differentiates.
[04:15] Aisha: procurement will still want a standard SOW with SLA language updated for the EU private region — is there a template?
[04:22] Priya: yes, we'll attach a template SOW and a proposed SLA addendum for EU region latency and uptime.
[04:29] Raj: ok next steps recap?
[04:33] Maya: sure — pricing worksheet + amendment draft by Friday, ops runbook and network diagram by Friday, Daniel to schedule perf soak for Tues/Wed, customer to provide SIEM endpoint + peak token load numbers by Monday, final sign target April 30.
[04:49] Sofia: sounds good. small note — for the perf soak we need 8 hours of steady load then a stress ramp to peak, is that the plan?
[04:58] Daniel: yes, we'll do a warmup, 8-hour steady, then 2-hour ramp to peak. we'll record metrics and provide a runbook snapshot.
[05:09] Luke: will we get a post-soak readout?
[05:12] Daniel: we'll send a readout and a config tweak plan if needed.
[05:20] Maya: any other questions?
[05:22] Raj: no, thanks all.
[05:25] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and the calendar invites.

Note: timestamps here are approximate; transcription contains some mis-heard words and shorthand typical of automated notes.

Customer to supply SIEM endpoints and peak load metrics
